title: Algorithms for Data Science
standfirst: The algorithmic ideas — sketching, streaming, sampling, spectral methods — behind large-scale data analysis.

description_paragraphs: This second-level graduate course provides a broad overview and develops the tools and methods needed to address large-scale problems arising in data science applications. This course is also offered as an elective for Degree level students
faculty: Prof. Arun Rajkumar, Wadhwani School of Data Science, IIT Madras

weeks_text.label: Week 1
weeks_text.text: Algorithms for data science; Concentration inequalities (Markov, Chebyshev, Hoeffding); Johnson-Lindenstrauss (JL) lemma foundations.

weeks_text.label: Week 2
weeks_text.text: JL lemma (proof and bounds); Linear algebra interpretation; Dimensionality reduction guarantees.

weeks_text.label: Week 3
weeks_text.text: Approximate nearest neighbors; Locality Sensitive Hashing (LSH); Hash design, collision analysis, TPR/FPR trade-offs.

weeks_text.label: Week 4
weeks_text.text: Singular Value Decomposition (SVD); Fast and randomized SVD; Applications in large-scale data.

weeks_text.label: Week 5
weeks_text.text: Clustering basics; Spectral clustering; Graph cuts and min-cut formulations.

weeks_text.label: Week 6
weeks_text.text: Scalable spectral clustering; Spectral sparsification; Large-scale clustering techniques.

weeks_text.label: Week 7
weeks_text.text: Statistical learning theory; Data distributions; Bayes classifier; Error decomposition.

weeks_text.label: Week 8
weeks_text.text: Generalization theory; Sample complexity; Bounds on learning performance.

weeks_text.label: Week 9
weeks_text.text: VC dimension; Hypothesis classes; Uniform convergence; Capacity of models.

weeks_text.label: Week 10
weeks_text.text: Learning theory recap; Estimation vs approximation error; Empirical risk minimization (ERM) and structural risk minimization (SRM); Sample compression.
